stages.name: trigger
stages.what: push to main or a pull_request event starts the workflow.
stages.why: Every change gets the same gates, whether or not a human remembers to run them.
stages.failures: A branch nobody pushes to a PR never gets checked.

stages.name: runner
stages.what: GitHub provisions a fresh ubuntu-latest VM (GitLab: python:3.12-bookworm container) with timeout-minutes: 10.
stages.why: A clean machine proves the repo is self-contained — nothing works 'because of my laptop'.
stages.failures: Dependencies not declared in pyproject.toml fail here even though they pass locally.

stages.name: install
stages.what: pip install -e '.[dev]' with pip caching keyed on the dependency files.
stages.why: The editable install is exactly what a new contributor does — CI tests the onboarding path too.
stages.failures: A stale cache is a rare but real source of 'works locally, red in CI'.

stages.name: quality gates
stages.what: ruff check → ruff format --check → mypy → pytest, each exiting nonzero on failure.
stages.why: The runner sees only exit codes; every tool's exit status is a contract.
stages.failures: Piping a command can hide its exit code — the pipeline's truth is the step's exit status.

stages.name: artifacts
stages.what: upload-artifact with if: always() ships evidence/ (JUnit, DUT log, coverage) even when a step failed.
stages.why: Failures are exactly when you need the logs. always() is the difference between diagnosable and guesswork.
stages.failures: if-no-files-found: error turns 'evidence silently missing' into a loud failure.
